messages.subject: Error with "count" output
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I"m trying to write a count detection history to later use as an index covariate. I have run the code succesfully to make a binary detection history with no problem. The only thing I change is output=c("binary") to output=c("count") with all the rest of the code identical. I end up with an error saying

 "Error in record.hist[match(names(occasions.by.station)[xyz], rownames(record.hist)),  :
  number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length"

The camOp file, input file, and everything is the same but I keep getting this error and it prevents a detection history from being produced.

Here's the rest of the code in case it helps
detectionHistory(recordTable = CL, species = "clouded leopard",
                 camOp = camOp, output = c("count"), stationCol = "station",
                 speciesCol ="species", recordDateTimeCol ="vid_date",
                 recordDateTimeFormat = "%Y-%m-%d", occasionLength = 30,
                 day1 = "2015-07-01", includeEffort = TRUE, scaleEffort = FALSE,
                 occasionStartTime = 0,datesAsOccasionNames = TRUE,  timeZone ="Pacific/Johnston",
                 writecsv = TRUE, outDir =("C:/Users/selwynra/Desktop/analysis/output/30 day"),
                 unmarkedMultFrameInput = FALSE)

Does anyone have any idea what might be causing this?

cheers,
-Rachel

messages.subject: Re: Is there a way to set occasion length = a month not # of days?
messages.subject_clean: Is there a way to set occasion length = a month not # of days?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rachel,
Here is a possible workaround. The idea is to create separate detection histories with different occasion lengths for each month, then combine them all into one. For every month, change 2 arguments: occasionLength and day1.

Some caveats here:
- in the first month, set day1 to the day the first camera was set up, and set occasionLength so that the occasion ends on the last day of the month (check column names in resulting detection history)
- the  proposed workaround only works if there is at least one record at any station in a given month. Otherwise, there will be an error to avoid returning an empty detection history (this is why below i added a record manually)
- I would have liked to include the argument maxNumberDays in detectionHistory, but that didn't work due to a bug. I'll investigate and update when I know more.
- if your study covered many months, you might wish to automate this using e.g. a for loop.

Here's a example based on the sample data in the package.

# load station information
data(camtraps)

# create camera operation matrix
camop_no_problem <- cameraOperation(CTtable      = camtraps,
                                    stationCol   = "Station",
                                    setupCol     = "Setup_date",
                                    retrievalCol = "Retrieval_date",
                                    hasProblems  = FALSE,
                                    dateFormat   = "%d/%m/%Y"
)

data(recordTableSample)    # load the record history, as created above

# add a record in May, so function doesn't fail

rowToAdd <- recordTableSample[5,]
rowToAdd$DateTimeOriginal <- "2009-05-10 05:07:00"   # add 1 month to the date
recordTableSample <- rbind(recordTableSample,
                           rowToAdd)

# Detection history April
DetHist_2009_04 <- detectionHistory(recordTable         = recordTableSample,
                             camOp                = camop_no_problem,
                             stationCol           = "Station",
                             speciesCol           = "Species",
                             recordDateTimeCol    = "DateTimeOriginal",
                             species              = "VTA",
                             occasionLength       = 29,
                             day1                 = "2009-04-02",
                             datesAsOccasionNames = TRUE,
                             includeEffort        = TRUE,
                             scaleEffort          = FALSE,
                             timeZone             = "Asia/Kuala_Lumpur"
)

# Detection history May
DetHist_2009_05 <- detectionHistory(recordTable          = recordTableSample,
                                    camOp                = camop_no_problem,
                                    stationCol           = "Station",
                                    speciesCol           = "Species",
                                    recordDateTimeCol    = "DateTimeOriginal",
                                    species              = "VTA",
                                    occasionLength       = 31,
                                    day1                 = "2009-05-01",
                                    datesAsOccasionNames = TRUE,
                                    includeEffort        = TRUE,
                                    scaleEffort          = FALSE,
                                    timeZone             = "Asia/Kuala_Lumpur"
)

DetHist_2009_04
DetHist_2009_05

# make list of detection histories and effort matrices
DetHistList <- list(DetHist_2009_04$detection_history,
                    DetHist_2009_05$detection_history)
EffortList <- list(DetHist_2009_04$effort,
                   DetHist_2009_05$effort)

# take the first column of each, preserving proper column and row names
DetHist_tmp <- lapply(DetHistList, FUN = function(x) {
  y <- matrix(x[, 1], ncol = 1)
  colnames(y) <- colnames(x)[1]
  rownames(y) <- rownames(x)
  data.frame(y, check.names = FALSE)
  y
  })

Effort_tmp <- lapply(EffortList, FUN = function(x) {
  y <- matrix(x[, 1], ncol = 1)
  colnames(y) <- colnames(x)[1]
  rownames(y) <- rownames(x)
  data.frame(y, check.names = FALSE)
  y
  })

# combine into single data frame
dethist_combined <- do.call(cbind, DetHist_tmp)
effort_combined  <- do.call(cbind, Effort_tmp)

# check results
dethist_combined
effort_combined

> dethist_combined
         2009-04-02_2009-04-30 2009-05-01_2009-05-17
StationA                     1                     1
StationB                     1                     0
StationC                     1                     0
> effort_combined
         2009-04-02_2009-04-30 2009-05-01_2009-05-17
StationA                    29                    14
StationB                    28                    16
StationC                    27                    17

messages.subject: Re: Error setting eventSummaryColumn when running recordtable function
messages.subject_clean: Error setting eventSummaryColumn when running recordtable function
messages.body_plain:
Hi Belén,
are you getting an error or a warning? It should normally be a warning only and still return the record table. Does it?
The warning is supposed to show when you wish to return statistics for a column (Individuos in your example) that is not found in the metadata of the images at a particular station. Did you maybe not assign the "Individuos" tag at some stations?
If you assigned it at all stations, we'll need to investigate further.
Thank you,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: Error with "count" output
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
thank you for the data. The problem was that in your example the record date/time was defined as date only:

recordDateTimeCol ="vid_date",
recordDateTimeFormat = "%Y-%m-%d"

At one station there was a record on the day the first station was set up. The time difference of that record relative to the camera setup was thus calculated as 0, which made camtrapR try to assign that record to column 0 in the detection matrix. And of course there is not column 0.

The fix was to combine record date and time, which leads to time differences greater than 0.

rec$DateTime <- paste(rec$vid_date, rec$vid_time)

and use that in

detectionHistory(..., recordDateTimeCol = "DateTime",
                      recordDateTimeFormat = "dmy HMS")

Interesting issue. I will change the package accordingly and at least give users a warning in the future.
Thank you for bringing it up.
Best regards,
Jürgen
